problem: Conversational AI agents powered by LLMs fail reliably when encountering unanticipated user-induced errors and cannot recover without retraining or prompt modifications.
approach: Reasoning Inception (ReIn) uses an external module to identify predefined dialogue errors and generate recovery plans, which are integrated into the agent's internal reasoning to guide corrective actions without altering model parameters.
contribution: ReIn substantially improves task success and generalizes to unseen error types while outperforming explicit prompt-modification approaches across diverse agent models and inception module combinations.

problem: Vision-language models remain vulnerable to cross-modal adversarial attacks, especially when function words in language interfere with the robustness of the visual-semantic alignment.
approach: Function-word De-Attention (FDA) calculates differential cross-attention within heads to suppress the impact of function words, similar to a differential amplifier, creating more robust multimodal representations.
contribution: FDA achieves 18-53% adversarial success rate drops with minimal performance drops (0.2-0.6%) on retrieval tasks and a 90% ASR drop with 0.3% performance gain on visual grounding across multiple models.

problem: Large language models trained on nearly all available data inevitably memorize sensitive training information, amplifying privacy leakage risks that current membership inference attacks fail to fully quantify.
approach: InfoRMIA reformulates membership inference through an information-theoretic lens and introduces token-level analysis to localize memorized content from the sequence level down to individual tokens.
contribution: InfoRMIA outperforms the state-of-the-art RMIA method while offering improved computational efficiency and enables pinpointing which tokens are memorized within generated outputs.

problem: Existing vision-language models lack unified multilingual and cross-modal support, forcing separate training pipelines and limiting generalization across languages and modalities.
approach: vSONAR extends the SONAR text embedding space with a post-hoc alignment pipeline that maps vision encoder representations into the SONAR space, enabling unified vision-language modeling across 200 text and 37 speech languages.
contribution: vLCM (vision-extended Large Concept Model) matches state-of-the-art vision-language models on image/video captioning and QA while significantly outperforming them across 61 out of 62 tested languages.

problem: LLMs respond with substantially less preference variation than humans, and existing preference collection methods fail to capture the diversity of human values across cultural and political dimensions.
approach: Community Alignment uses negatively-correlated sampling to generate diverse candidate responses, enabling preference learning methods to capture heterogeneous preferences within a large-scale multilingual and multi-turn dataset.
contribution: Community Alignment collects 233,319 comparisons from annotators spanning five countries, demonstrating that negatively-correlated sampling significantly enhances alignment methods' effectiveness in learning diverse human preferences.

problem: Existing physics benchmarks evaluate only final answers and rely on heuristic LLM-as-judge scoring, failing to capture reasoning processes and provide reliable diagnostic feedback for process-level understanding.
approach: PRISM-Physics represents solutions as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of formulas encoding causal dependencies between steps, paired with rule-based symbolic formula equivalence matching for consistent validation without heuristics.
contribution: PRISM-Physics provides theoretically grounded process-level evaluation aligned with human expert scoring and reveals persistent reasoning failures in state-of-the-art LLMs on physics problems.

problem: Real-time motion-controllable video generation faces latency constraints from bidirectional diffusion models and lacks effective autoregressive approaches that support diverse motion control without quality degradation.
approach: AR-Drag combines autoregressive video diffusion with reinforcement learning and a trajectory-based reward model, using a Self-Rollout mechanism to preserve the Markov property while accelerating training.
contribution: AR-Drag achieves high visual fidelity and precise motion alignment with 1.3B parameters, reducing latency significantly compared to state-of-the-art motion-controllable video diffusion models.

problem: Text-based table retrieval methods flatten tables into linear sequences, losing structural information and failing to handle embedded images or complex table layouts, compromising retrieval performance.
approach: TaR-ViR reformulates table retrieval as a multimodal task by treating tables as images, naturally preserving structural and content information while being format-agnostic.
contribution: The TaR-ViR benchmark and image-based table retrieval paradigm achieve more effective and efficient retrieval by leveraging visual representations that inherently preserve table structure.

problem: Virtual try-off systems that generate standardized product images from clothed individuals suffer from visual ambiguity and severely degraded details, limiting their practical applicability.
approach: TEMU-VTOFF uses a dual DiT-based architecture with modified multimodal attention incorporating image, text, and mask information, plus an alignment module to refine visual details for high fidelity.
contribution: TEMU-VTOFF achieves state-of-the-art performance on VITON-HD and Dress Code datasets, significantly improving both visual quality and fidelity compared to existing virtual try-off methods.

problem: Existing mixture-of-experts approaches for parameter-efficient LLM adaptation rely on conventional TopK routing requiring careful hyperparameter tuning and assigning a fixed number of experts per token.
approach: LD-MoLE replaces non-differentiable TopK routing with a differentiable routing function and closed-form solution, enabling adaptive, token-dependent, and layer-wise expert allocation with analytical sparsity control.
contribution: LD-MoLE achieves superior performance on diverse benchmarks across Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-3B while learning token-dependent and layer-wise expert allocation patterns.

problem: Conformal prediction methods rely on residual-based scores that impose geometric constraints and struggle with multimodal distributions, producing overly conservative prediction areas centered around the mean.
approach: JAPAN uses normalizing flows to estimate predictive density and constructs prediction areas by thresholding on density scores, enabling compact, potentially disjoint, and context-adaptive regions with finite-sample coverage guarantees.
contribution: JAPAN demonstrates good calibration and tighter prediction areas compared to existing baselines on multivariate regression and forecasting tasks while retaining finite-sample validity.

problem: Diffusion transformers for video generation require prohibitive computational and memory resources that hinder practical deployment, and naive combinations of quantization and sparsification cause performance degradation.
approach: QuantSparse integrates model quantization with attention sparsification using Multi-Scale Salient Attention Distillation and Second-Order Sparse Attention Reparameterization to mitigate quantization-induced bias.
contribution: QuantSparse on HunyuanVideo-13B achieves 20.88 PSNR with 3.68× storage reduction and 1.88× inference acceleration, substantially outperforming the quantization baseline Q-VDiT.

problem: Genomic Foundation Models trained with NLP-style pretraining show unclear relationships between pretraining performance and downstream task effectiveness, raising questions about pretraining cost-efficiency.
approach: A comprehensive evaluation compares seven GFMs across 52 diverse genomic tasks against randomly initialized baselines, analyzing how tokenizer and architecture choices affect both baselines and pretraining gains.
contribution: Character-token models match or exceed larger pretrained k-mer/BPE models on many tasks; GFMs fail to capture clinically relevant mutations, suggesting current pretraining provides modest, tokenizer-dependent improvements.

problem: Existing hand-object interaction generation is constrained to fixed grasping patterns and cannot capture the diversity of free-form daily interactions like pushing, poking, and rotating.
approach: TOUCH uses a three-stage multi-level diffusion model with fine-grained semantic control and explicit contact modeling, refined with contact consistency and physical constraints to generate diverse hand interactions.
contribution: TOUCH generates controllable, diverse, and physically plausible hand-object interactions for 4.4k unique interactions across 92 intents and 403 object categories, extending beyond traditional grasping.

problem: Machine unlearning fails when retained samples closely relate to the forget set through correlated features or semantic similarities, leading to unintentional performance degradation on related data.
approach: A two-phase optimization framework first increases forget-set loss while preserving less-related retained accuracy, then applies gradient projection regularized by Wasserstein-2 distance to mitigate performance degradation on semantically related samples.
contribution: The proposed method achieves effective and reliable unlearning while outperforming baselines in both accuracy retention and removal fidelity across multiple tasks and architectures.

problem: Out-of-distribution generalization methods struggle with datasets containing heterogeneous causal subgraphs at the instance level, requiring either risky data augmentation or questionable causal assumptions.
approach: A Mixture-of-Experts framework enforces semantic diversity among experts each generating distinct causal subgraphs while a learned gate assigns sparse weights, adaptively focusing on relevant experts without requiring environment labels.
contribution: The framework achieves strong performance on the GOOD benchmark across synthetic and real-world structural shifts by modeling instance-level heterogeneity through diverse, sparse expert selection.

problem: Textual feedback propagation in long-horizon compound AI systems suffers from exploding textual gradients and vanishing signals as feedback traverses multiple hops, limiting optimization of deep agentic workflows.
approach: Textual Equilibrium Propagation uses local iterative prompt refinement in a free phase followed by bounded proximal prompt edits with forward signaling in a nudged phase, avoiding deep backward feedback chains.
contribution: TEP supports local prompt optimization with controlled adaptation toward global goals on long-horizon QA benchmarks and multi-agent tool-use datasets without the degradation of global textual backpropagation.

problem: Learning to Defer systems fail to generalize to unseen experts who are out-of-distribution relative to the training population because they learn identity-conditioned policies that violate permutation symmetry.
approach: Identity-Free Deferral enforces permutation symmetry by building query-independent Bayesian competence profiles and supplying only structural information (model confidence, expert skill) while obscuring class identities.
contribution: IFD consistently improves generalization to unseen experts on medical imaging benchmarks and ImageNet-16H with real human annotators by removing identity conditioning shortcuts.

problem: LoRA-sharing platforms pose unexamined jailbreak and backdoor risks when downloaded adapters balance task utility against attack objectives, potentially compromising model safety across downstream applications.
approach: JailbreakLoRA uses multi-task training balancing task utility and attack capability through uncertainty-weighted losses and gradient conflict mitigation, generating affirmative prefixes on trigger activation.
contribution: JailbreakLoRA achieves 16% improvement in attack success rate while enhancing multi-downstream task performance by 16.5% on average, demonstrating effective dual-objective attacks on LoRA adapters.

problem: Machine learning for tandem-airfoil flow field prediction lacks adequate benchmark datasets and evaluation on multi-body configurations compared to single-airfoil approaches.
approach: TandemFoilSet provides five tandem-airfoil datasets paired with four single-airfoil counterparts using curriculum learning, directional integrated distance representation, residual pre-training, and domain decomposition.
contribution: TandemFoilSet comprises 8,104 CFD simulations total and demonstrates notable gains in flow prediction accuracy through curriculum and domain decomposition strategies.

problem: Clinical ICU data comprises heterogeneous multivariate time series sampled irregularly with pervasive missingness, yet existing models struggle to balance accuracy and interpretability for outcome prediction.
approach: GARLIC imputes missing data via exponential-decay encoding, captures inter-sensor dependencies through time-lagged summary graphs, and fuses patterns with cross-dimensional attention, with all weights and edges learned end-to-end for interpretability.
contribution: GARLIC achieves state-of-the-art AUROC and AUPRC on three ICU benchmarks (PhysioNet 2012/2019, MIMIC-III) while providing transparent, verifiable importance attribution through feature-removal trials.

problem: Deploying large language models under diverse resource constraints requires training multiple independent model sizes, which is prohibitively expensive and provides only coarse-grained size options.
approach: Boomerang distillation distills from a large teacher to a small student, then progressively reconstructs intermediate sizes by re-incorporating teacher layer blocks without additional training.
contribution: Boomerang distillation generates zero-shot fine-grained model families whose performance scales smoothly between student and teacher, often matching or surpassing independently trained models of the same size.

problem: Table understanding approaches struggle to balance semantic and structural information, either losing structural cues through text-flattening or sacrificing semantic precision through image-only methods.
approach: TableDART uses a lightweight MLP gating network that dynamically selects between Text-only, Image-only, or Fusion paths for each table-query pair, mediated by a cross-modal agent that synthesizes outputs without full MLLM fine-tuning.
contribution: TableDART achieves state-of-the-art performance on seven benchmarks among open-source models by routing to appropriate modalities and avoiding redundancy and conflicts between textual and visual views.

problem: Conventional video diffusion models use scalar timestep variables that rigidly synchronize frame evolution, limiting fine-grained temporal control and requiring task-specific retraining or narrow applicability.
approach: Pusa V1.0 uses vectorized timestep adaptation (VTA) to enable non-destructive temporal control within a unified framework, achieving zero-shot image-to-video, video extension, and start-end frame tasks without task-specific training.
contribution: Pusa achieves comparable image-to-video results to fine-tuned alternatives in a zero-shot manner while unlocking multiple zero-shot capabilities and preserving base text-to-video capabilities.

problem: Causal discovery methods assume static graphs, but real-world systems exhibit dynamic causal relationships that vary with underlying parameters, limiting applicability to critical domains like industrial control.
approach: A novel framework models each causal link as a function of measurable system parameters using Polynomial Chaos Expansions (PCE), enabling tractable learning of functional causal structure from observational data.
contribution: On a large-scale chemical reactor dataset, the framework learns dynamic causal structure with 90.9% F1-score, nearly doubling baseline performance and providing interpretable models of causal mechanism evolution.

problem: The community lacks a comprehensive reasoning-centric benchmark to systematically evaluate unified multimodal models' alignment between understanding and generation capabilities on complex visual tasks.
approach: GIR-Bench evaluates unified models across three complementary perspectives: consistent knowledge leverage (GIR-Bench-Uni), reasoning-driven text-to-image generation (GIR-Bench-T2I), and multi-step reasoning editing (GIR-Bench-Edit).
contribution: GIR-Bench reveals that unified models remain persistently behind on reasoning-driven visual generation despite being more capable than generation-only systems, identifying a key performance gap.

problem: Contrastive learning's theoretical foundations remain underexplored, leaving questions about why certain pair-sampling strategies succeed and how they contribute to model performance unanswered.
approach: SPACL prioritizes hard positive and hard negative samples during pair construction and loss computation based on optimality analysis, providing theoretical grounding for sample selection strategies.
contribution: SPACL consistently outperforms or competes favorably with state-of-the-art methods across downstream tasks, validating theoretical insights through comprehensive ablations of its individual components.

problem: Vision models trained for generalization across diverse environments sacrifice performance on specific deployment scenarios, yet many practical applications operate in a single test environment and don't need broad generalization.
approach: Self-supervised pretraining using only rich multimodal data from the test environment enables representation learning without external internet-scale datasets, substituting scale with multimodality.
contribution: Test-environment pretraining with multimodal data matches and often outperforms generalist models pretrained on large-scale internet datasets (CLIP, DINOv2) on semantic segmentation, captioning, and object detection tasks.

problem: Open-vocabulary object detection models suffer sharp performance degradation under out-of-distribution domain shifts when adapting to new tasks while retaining pre-trained capabilities across diverse task orders.
approach: ABME uses model editing to inject new task knowledge via compact key-value representations and automatically balances new and old knowledge through stored KV matrices for order-agnostic task handling.
contribution: ABME achieves better retain-adapt trade-offs than continual learning approaches for open-vocabulary object detection while supporting order-agnostic task insertion/removal without retraining.

problem: Transformers' capabilities in unsupervised learning remain largely unexplored despite their success in supervised in-context learning and other downstream tasks.
approach: TGMM evaluates transformers on Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) and proves that transformers can efficiently approximate both the Expectation-Maximization algorithm and cubic tensor power iterations used in spectral methods.
contribution: Transformers effectively solve GMMs and mitigate limitations of classical methods like EM while exhibiting reasonable robustness to distribution shifts, providing first theoretical guarantees for high-order tensor operations.

problem: Diffusion model representation quality varies across layers but lacks mechanisms to leverage rich intermediate representations for guidance, missing opportunities for training efficiency improvements.
approach: LayerSync regularizes diffusion models using their own intermediate representations as intrinsic guidance, where the most semantically rich representations guide weaker ones without external supervision.
contribution: LayerSync speeds up flow-based transformer training by 8.75× on ImageNet and improves generation quality by 23.6%, generalizing across visual, audio, video, and motion domains with no pretrained models required.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization suffers from the squeezing effect where preferred response probabilities unintentionally decrease during training due to high-curvature expansion in logit space.
approach: Logits-SAM applies Sharpness-Aware Minimization only to the output layer as a computationally efficient variant that suppresses curvature expansion and regularizes coordinate-wise dynamics in logit space.
contribution: Logits-SAM consistently improves DPO effectiveness on Pythia-2.8B and Mistral-7B across multiple datasets with negligible computational overhead.

problem: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards suffers from limited trajectory diversity in group rollouts where local token-level stochasticity collapses into near-identical reasoning paths, hindering policy learning.
approach: Lookahead Tree-Based Rollouts iteratively branches at high-uncertainty steps, performs lookahead simulation for each branch, and prunes branches exhibiting prolonged similarity to enforce trajectory-level diversity.
contribution: LATR accelerates policy learning by 131% and improves pass@1 performance by 4.2% on GRPO and DAPO across reasoning tasks compared to stochastic sampling.

problem: Recent generative frameworks like diffusion and flow matching struggle to model integer-valued count data and systematically deconvolve aggregated observations in biology without principled approaches.
approach: Count Bridges introduce stochastic bridge processes on integers providing exact, tractable diffusion analogues with closed-form conditionals, extended to aggregated measurements via Expectation-Maximization treating unit-level counts as latent.
contribution: Count Bridges demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on integer distribution matching and enable principled deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq into single-cell profiles and resolution of multicellular spatial transcriptomic spots.

problem: Large reasoning models deploy multi-step reasoning guided by reflection tokens whose frequency and placement significantly impact performance, yet optimal reflection token usage remains unaddressed.
approach: Cyclical reflection token scheduling dynamically modulates reflection token logits with a bidirectional triangular waveform to adaptively regulate frequency and placement, treating tokens as an allocatable resource.
contribution: Cyclical scheduling improves performance across model sizes (1.5B-8B) on MATH500, AIME, AMC, GPQA, and LiveCodeBench, outperforming standard decoding and recent approaches like TIP without additional computation.

problem: Reinforcement learning action spaces vary widely (discrete, continuous, hybrid) requiring separate algorithms, and learning the critic over diverse action parameterizations poses theoretical and practical challenges.
approach: DA-PG treats action distributions as actions to unify action spaces and learns a generalized deterministic policy gradient with lower variance; DA-AC uses interpolated critic learning (ICL) to enhance learning over distribution parameters.
contribution: DA-AC achieves competitive performance across discrete, continuous, and hybrid control tasks on standard benchmarks by elegantly unifying diverse action space formulations.

problem: Transformer decoders' KV cache memory requirements become prohibitive at long sequence lengths, and existing cross-layer sharing methods underperform within-layer approaches like GQA.
approach: FusedKV learns to fuse informative KV caches from bottom and middle layers into top-layer representations; FusedKV-Lite directly derives top-layer values from bottom-layer values and middle-layer keys.
contribution: FusedKV reduces cache memory by 50% while achieving lower validation perplexity than standard Transformer decoders across LLMs ranging from 332M to 4B parameters.

problem: Existing multi-state protein design approaches rely on post-hoc aggregation of single-state predictions, achieving poor experimental success rates compared to single-state design.
approach: DynamicMPNN is an inverse folding model explicitly trained to generate sequences compatible with multiple conformations through joint learning across conformational ensembles.
contribution: DynamicMPNN outperforms ProteinMPNN by up to 25% on decoy-normalized RMSD and by 12% on sequence recovery across multi-state protein benchmarks when evaluated using AlphaFold 3.

problem: Diffusion LLMs exhibit hallucination that emerges throughout the multi-step denoising process, yet existing detection methods designed for auto-regressive LLMs fail to leverage the full temporal progression.
approach: TraceDet models the denoising process as an action trace and identifies the sub-trace maximally informative to hallucinated responses, leveraging key signals across the multi-step denoising process.
contribution: TraceDet consistently improves hallucination detection with an average AUROC gain of 15.2% compared to baselines across various open-source diffusion LLMs.

problem: Existing MLLMs evaluation benchmarks lack comprehensive assessment of human-centric scene understanding, failing to capture both granular perception and higher-dimensional causal reasoning about people.
approach: Human-MME provides rigorously curated evaluation across 4 primary visual domains with 15 secondary domains, featuring 19,945 image question pairs with progressive evaluation dimensions from granular to causal reasoning.
contribution: Human-MME's high-quality annotations with diverse data paradigms and 43 sub-fields enable precise assessment of MLLMs on human-centric scene understanding spanning multi-person and multi-image reasoning.
